qt: to the Commission Katri Kulmuni (Renew) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2023/15421 sets lithium recovery targets of 50 % by the end of 2027 and 80 % by the end of 2031. Mechanical recycling does not recover lithium, which requires downstream processing. While Europe has battery pre-treatment capacity, significant investment is still needed for competitive lithium recovery. Given lithium’s relatively low share of battery content and the concentration of competitive downstream capacity in Asia, battery recycling materials processed in the EU risk being exported for further treatment. This could undermine existing European recycling value chains for other critical raw materials, including cobalt, and reduce the use of established downstream capacity. 1.
How has the Commission assessed the targets’ impact on existing European battery recycling value chains, particularly those recovering other critical raw materials such as cobalt?
How will it address the shortage of competitive lithium recovery capacity in the EU and the risk of increased exports of battery recycling materials to third countries?
Does it consider that a review of the targets or their implementation is necessary to ensure they do not undermine existing European recycling infrastructure and value chains?

Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 July 2023 concerning batteries and waste batteries, amending Directive 2008/98/EC and Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and repealing Directive 2006/66/EC, OJ L 191, 28.7.2023, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1542/oj. 1
